data.narrative:
Exowatt is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Hannan Happi and Jack Abraham that has raised $90M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes nine peer companies—one public (LNZA) and eight private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—though no sufficiently narrow peer subset exists at the same stage and valuation tier to support a reliable median multiple.

Given data constraints, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using the $90M in total raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields $180M. This represents the most defensible quantitative anchor available.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $153M (low) to $207M (high), with a median point of $180M. The $27M spread reflects reasonable variance around stage-typical step-up dynamics. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer comparables at identical stage and tier, which limits confidence in both the multiplier selection and any cross-check against market precedent. Additional color on unit economics, customer traction, or capital efficiency would be necessary to refine this range materially.
